column1: # REACHABILITY OVER THE ENTITY GRAPH (the review's finding J,
# use-cases/REVIEW.md): "ship a transitive `reaches(a, b)` check verb".
# `relation` rows ask about the edge set as a whole. These ask the
# question that needs the CLOSURE -- does anything `a` links to, at any
# remove, end up at `b`? -- which is the shape of every blast-radius
# question an operator asks and every containment question a policy
# asks, and which cannot be put one edge at a time.
# A VERB and not a constraint, for the reason acyclicity is one:
# reachability is global and non-monotone, so a lattice citizen
# asserting NON-reachability could be true and then false as one more
# edge arrives.
# TRANSITIVE, NOT REFLEXIVE-TRANSITIVE: `a` reaches itself only through
# a cycle, which is the useful answer rather than the vacuous one. The
# path reported is a SHORTEST one, and among shortest ones the first in
# code-point order, so it is the same path in both ports.
# Columns: name<TAB>reaches<TAB>src<TAB>expect, where expect carries the
# question under `ask` ({from, to, relation?}) beside the report.
# Every expectation here was obtained by running BOTH engines and
# diffing, never by copying one.
reaches-through-a-chain
reaches-one-edge
unreachable-no-path
unreachable-wrong-way
not-reflexive-without-a-cycle
reaches-itself-through-a-cycle
relation-filter-follows-one-relation
relation-filter-absent-follows-every-edge
shortest-path-is-the-one-reported
an-address-reaches-the-node-it-names
an-address-does-not-reach-the-node-above-it
endpoint-that-names-nothing-is-a-refusal
# A document that does not stand up is not a document with an
# unreachable pair, and two links to the same place are one
# successor -- the search must not walk it twice. Parity-probed.
a-document-that-does-not-stand-up-has-no-graph
a-repeated-edge-is-one-successor
# ENDPOINTS ARE PATHS (ADR-014), and the grammar is checked before the
# graph is consulted. A path that names a real node with no edges is a
# perfectly good question with the answer `unreachable`; only one that
# names NOTHING refuses. The root is a legitimate endpoint -- a link at
# the top of a document starts there -- even though `$` is not a
# refer() target (refer.tsv, `address-root-alone`).
endpoint-inside-a-list
endpoint-is-the-root
endpoint-unanchored-is-a-refusal
endpoint-bad-segment-is-a-refusal
endpoint-through-a-scalar-is-a-refusal
